description: Authored map for scripts/ai-bio-admission.ts: which pack records each part admits, how each is corrected under the maintainer’s decisions of 2026-10-28 (review/ai-bio-pack-2026-10-28.md) and the cross-family check of 2026-10-30, and the records, documents, entities and sources added at admission. 1.snapshotDescription: Dataset state before part 1 of the AI and biosecurity admission (2026-10-30): the IDs it adds and the rows it changes as they were.
1.scope: On 2026-10-30, by the maintainer’s decisions of 2026-10-28 and the corrections of a blind cross-family check, the first part of a machine-prepared, machine-audited candidate pack on AI and biosecurity was admitted: the biological provisions of frontier AI framework editions, the United States, United Kingdom, European Union, Chinese and Biological Weapons Convention texts that address AI and biological risk, and the rules and guidance for screening synthetic nucleic acid orders, each recorded at policy level as its own text states it. Framework and instrument provisions describe what a text states, never implementation, compliance or effectiveness. Technical, procedural and screening-criterion content in every source was excluded by rule. Three framework editions that no retrieval here could open are recorded from the cross-family check’s reading of named archive captures, and say so. All records are seeds; none is human-reviewed.

2.snapshotDescription: Dataset state before part 2 of the AI and biosecurity admission (2026-10-30): the IDs it adds and the rows it changes as they were.
2.scope: On 2026-10-30 the second part of the AI and biosecurity admission added, under schema 2.22, what published reports state as the results of their own biological-capability evaluations, the institutes’ documented engagements with developers, and the arguments published for and against AI-related biological risk, as seven propositions with the texts that articulate, contest or bear on them. A stated result is the report’s own, for the system, version, sample and setting it names, with the caveats it gives; it is never a verified finding, never generalised, and a null or limiting result is not evidence that no effect exists. A record of a text’s stance on a proposition is never evidence that the proposition is true. Technical content in every source was excluded by rule. All records are seeds; none is human-reviewed.

hold.ab-ev-kimi-k2t-no-bio-evaluation: A recorded absence on a model card that states no date. The schema dates every provision record by one of its expression’s own dates, with a basis, so a snapshot provision cannot be admitted; this is the question part 1 left with the maintainer for four such records.

ab-scr-hhs-2010-effective-date.qualification: States the date the 2010 guidance gives for its own effect. The provision kind is `date`, added in schema 2.22 for a date a text states for its own application; part 1 recorded it as a threshold, on the dataset’s earlier precedent.

ab-scr-ostp-framework-funding-requiremen.qualificationAppend: The provision kind is now `date` (schema 2.22), where part 1 used `threshold` on the dataset’s earlier precedent.

ab-scr-hhs-2010-voluntary-all-providers.qualificationAppend: The provision kind is now `standing` (schema 2.22), the kind for the standing a text claims for itself, where part 1 used `exception`.

ab-fw-ms-fgf-2026-changelog-no-cbrn-entr.qualification: A recorded absence in one named part of one edition. It is not a finding that the CBRN thresholds are unchanged: this record does not compare the two editions’ Critical CBRN rows, and the pack’s record of that comparison is not admitted here. It says nothing about other parts of the edition or about practice.
ab-fw-ms-fgf-2026-changelog-no-cbrn-entr.inferenceRationale: Premises: the inspected scope was the whole of Appendix II – Change log on PDF p. 16 (printed p. 15), whose February 2026 entry lists six changes. Method: the search terms “CBRN”, “chemical”, “biological” and “threshold” applied to the normalised text of the entry. The entry names the addition of harmful manipulation and loss of control as tracked high-risk capabilities, the update cadence, the scope of the framework, the cadence of deeper capability assessment, a definition of substantially fine-tuned models, and other edits for clarity. The record means not found within that scope.

ab-scr-hhs-2022-draft-published.statement: The Office of the Assistant Secretary for Preparedness and Response published a proposed revised screening framework guidance for providers and users of synthetic oligonucleotides in the Federal Register of 29 April 2022, submitting it for public consideration and comment for a period of 60 days.
ab-scr-hhs-2022-draft-published.qualificationAppend: The notice of April 2022 prints the submitting body as the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Preparedness and Response, and the statement uses that name (cross-family check, item 26). The dataset entity carries the later Administration name, which the 2023 notice and the component’s current pages use; no text stating a renaming was retrieved, so no dated name is recorded and the question is listed in the admission record.

ab-scr-ostp-framework-scope.statement: The Framework states that it applies to federally funded life sciences research involving the procurement of all types of synthetic nucleic acids that contain a synthetic sequence within the category the framework defines, and of any benchtop equipment capable of synthesising nucleic acids, and to distribution by providers including biofoundries, cloud laboratories, institutions with core synthesis facilities and contract research organisations, and by manufacturers of benchtop equipment.
ab-scr-ostp-framework-scope.qualificationAppend: That limitation was restored to the statement and to the paraphrase at admission, at policy level (cross-family check, item 68).

ab-scr-igsc-hsp-v31-refusal-reporting.statement: Version 3.1 of the Harmonized Screening Protocol states that members reserve the right to refuse to fill any order and to notify other members, law enforcement or other authorities on identifying potentially problematic orders, and that a reporting duty applies to requests within a category of sequences the protocol defines, received from a suspicious potential customer or from one that fails to establish legitimacy under the protocol’s customer-screening practices.
ab-scr-igsc-hsp-v31-refusal-reporting.qualificationAppend: The reporting duty is bounded to a defined category of requests, not to every request from such a customer (cross-family check, item 75); the category itself is a screening criterion and is not recorded.

time.note: Dated by the revision of September 2024, the expression in which the wording was checked. The framework was first released on 29 April 2024, and the April edition was not retrieved, so that release is not treated as authenticating this wording.

ab-scr-ostp-framework-eo14110-link.qualificationAppend: The record is dated by the September 2024 revision rather than the April 2024 release, because the April edition was not retrieved (cross-family check, widened review of this source family).

ab-scr-ostp-framework-funding-requiremen.qualificationAppend: The record is dated by the expression that states the requirement, the revision of September 2024, because the schema dates a provision by one of its expression’s own dates. The day the framework states for application to purchases, 26 April 2025, is in the statement and in the quoted passage; it is not an effective date of any agency’s own terms and conditions.

ab-scr-igsc-hsp-v31-screening-validation.qualificationAppend: The locator was corrected at admission: requirement 2.6 is on PDF p. 14 (cross-family check, widened review of this source family).

ab-arg-b5-soice-articulates.qualification: The record documents what this preprint proposes; it is not evidence that screening is effective, that any provider screens, or that the proposition is true. It holds no earliest-located role: the passage does not meet the proposition’s criterion.
ab-arg-b5-soice-articulates.statement: The preprint of 6 June 2023 states that promising nonproliferation measures include pre-release evaluations of language models by third parties, curation of training datasets, and verifiable screening of all DNA generated by synthesis providers.
ab-arg-b5-soice-articulates.missing: The passage proposes screening among three promising measures; it does not state that mitigation of AI-related biological risk depends on screening, which is the proposition’s criterion.
ab-arg-b5-soice-articulates.qualificationAppend: Downgraded at admission from the role the pack gave it, on the cross-family check of 2026-10-30: the passage does not meet the proposition’s criterion as worded. The record keeps the passage and says what it lacks. (item 98).

ab-arg-b7-sandbrink-articulates.qualification: The record documents what version 1 of this preprint states; it is not evidence that the proposition is true and implies no influence between texts. It holds no earliest-located role: the passage does not meet the proposition’s criterion.
ab-arg-b7-sandbrink-articulates.missing: The passage states that design tools expand the capabilities of sophisticated actors and proposes interventions aimed at them; it does not state that assessment must cover actors who already hold relevant skills, which is the proposition’s criterion.
ab-arg-b7-sandbrink-articulates.qualificationAppend: Downgraded at admission from the role the pack gave it, on the cross-family check of 2026-10-30: the passage does not meet the proposition’s criterion as worded. The record keeps the passage and says what it lacks. (item 102).

ab-arg-b5-moulange-contests.qualification: The record documents a possibility this paper states at the generality of its own abstract; it is not evidence that screening has been evaded, that any system is evadable, or that the proposition is false. No method of evasion is recorded. It holds no contesting or earliest-located role: the passage does not meet what the contesting relation requires.
ab-arg-b5-moulange-contests.missing: The passage states that the design capabilities could be used to evade screening; it does not contest screening’s role as a control point on which mitigation depends, which the contesting relation would require.
ab-arg-b5-moulange-contests.qualificationAppend: Downgraded at admission from the role the pack gave it, on the cross-family check of 2026-10-30: the passage does not meet the proposition’s criterion as worded. The record keeps the passage and says what it lacks. (item 105).

ab-arg-b5-sandbrink-articulates.qualificationAppend: This record holds the earliest located articulation from admission on 2026-10-30: the earlier passage the pack headlined does not meet the criterion (cross-family check, item 98), and this one states that reducing the risks depends on enhanced screening. The replaced headline stays on record as a correction.

ab-arg-b7-brent-articulates.qualificationAppend: This record holds the earliest located articulation from admission on 2026-10-30: the earlier passage the pack headlined does not meet the criterion (cross-family check, item 102), and this one states that safety assessments fail to cover skilled actors. The replaced headline stays on record as a correction.

ab-arg-b1-soice-articulates.statement: The preprint “Can large language models democratize access to dual-use biotechnology?” (arXiv v1, 6 June 2023) states that its results suggest that large language models will make pandemic-class agents widely accessible as soon as they are credibly identified, even to people with little or no laboratory training.
ab-arg-b1-soice-articulates.qualificationAppend: The statement keeps the preprint’s own tentative wording and the condition it attaches, both restored at admission (cross-family check, item 96).

ab-ev-rand-redteam-no-difference.statement: RAND’s red-team study states that it found no statistically significant difference in the viability of the plans produced by its red cells with or without large language model assistance, for the two models and the twelve cells of its main comparison.
ab-ev-rand-redteam-no-difference.qualificationAppend: The main comparison uses twelve red cells; fifteen is the total including the exploratory cells, and the sample framing was corrected at admission (cross-family check, item 14).

newClaims.subject: meta-faf-v1-1

object.value: Chemical and biological risk in scope: capability-triggered red teaming and a release decision on residual risk

newClaims.statement: Frontier AI Framework v1.1 states that chemical and biological risks are within its scope, that red teaming is conducted when relevant capability levels are reached, with external experts where appropriate, and that a release decision is taken on the residual risk left after evaluations and mitigations, with leadership able to require further testing, information or mitigation first.

time.note: Provision as the edition states it, dated by the edition’s publication date, 3 February 2025, as the dataset records it. The capture read is of 13 February 2025.

newClaims.qualification: What the edition states, at policy level. It is not evidence of implementation, compliance or safeguard effectiveness, and it names no model. The edition was read only by the cross-family machine check of 2026-10-30, in the archive capture the source names; this admission could not reach the Internet Archive, so the reading is not independently repeated here. The provision kind is `statement`, the dataset’s kind for a document’s stated content, because the schema’s other kinds require a verbatim quotation of the edition and none could be taken.
newClaims.hazardNote: Policy-level provisions only; the edition’s threat-scenario and evaluation detail was excluded by the check and is not recorded.

object.value: Announced plans to reform the U.S. AI Safety Institute as the Center for AI Standards and Innovation

newClaims.statement: The Department of Commerce bulletin sent on 4 June 2025, carrying a release dated 3 June 2025, states that the Secretary of Commerce announced his plans to reform the agency formerly known as the U.S. AI Safety Institute into the Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI).

time.note: Dated by the bulletin’s own sent date; the release it carries is dated 3 June 2025.

newClaims.qualification: Announced plans, as the bulletin states them. It is not evidence that any reorganisation was completed, and no legal continuity or succession is recorded. The dataset already carries the Center for AI Standards and Innovation as a dated name of the institute from June 2025, on a later NIST editorial note; this record adds the Commerce statement itself, which the earlier pass could not retrieve.

ab-prop-current-system-uplift.name: Currently available AI systems increase an actor's biological-misuse capability
ab-prop-current-system-uplift.description: The record of a text's stance on it is never evidence that it is true.

proposition.criterion: The text states that AI systems already deployed or publicly available at the time of writing increase the ability of an actor seeking to cause biological harm, relative to the resources otherwise available to that actor.

ab-prop-physical-bottleneck.name: The binding barrier is physical execution rather than information
ab-prop-physical-bottleneck.description: Worded worded from the located texts rather than from a standard formulation. Recorded at the level of the texts' own abstracts, summaries and conclusions.

proposition.criterion: The text states that access to information is not the barrier that limits biological misuse, because what remains required is physical: acquiring materials and succeeding at hands-on laboratory work.

ab-prop-evaluation-validity.name: Published evaluations do not establish real-world biological risk
ab-prop-evaluation-validity.description: Texts that articulate it disagree with each other about the direction of the error.

proposition.criterion: The text states that published evaluations or benchmarks of AI systems' biological capability do not, as conducted, establish the level of real-world biological misuse risk.

ab-prop-design-tools-distinct.name: Biological design tools pose risks distinct from those of language models
ab-prop-design-tools-distinct.description: One proposition of the AI and biosecurity collection.

proposition.criterion: The text states that AI tools built to design or predict biological molecules or systems create misuse risks that differ in kind, in the actors they affect or in the governance they require, from those of general-purpose language models.

ab-prop-synthesis-screening-control-poin.name: Synthesis-order screening is a control point for AI-related biological risk
ab-prop-synthesis-screening-control-poin.description: Recorded at the policy level only; no record states how screening is performed or how it could fail.

proposition.criterion: The text states that screening orders for synthesised nucleic acids is a control point on which mitigation of AI-related biological risk depends.

ab-prop-open-weights-bio-risk.name: Public release of model weights increases biological misuse risk
ab-prop-open-weights-bio-risk.description: One proposition of the AI and biosecurity collection.

proposition.criterion: The text states that making model weights publicly available increases the risk of biological misuse, or that some models should for that reason not be released openly.

ab-prop-skilled-actor-scope.name: Assessment must cover actors who already hold relevant skills
ab-prop-skilled-actor-scope.description: It concerns the scope of assessment, not the size of any risk.

proposition.criterion: The text states that assessment of AI-related biological risk must cover actors who already hold relevant scientific skills, and not only actors without them.
